issues.legal_issue: The existence of a civil suit concerning the same transaction does not, by itself, justify quashing a criminal case where the alleged conduct may also constitute criminal offences.
The power to initiate criminal proceedings for offences under the general penal law is independent of an authority’s power to cancel registration of documents.
Section 83 of the Registration Act permits a Sub-Registrar in whose territory an offence was committed to commence a prosecution, or to do so with the specified authority’s permission.

A court exercising inherent powers to quash an FIR must assess whether a prima facie offence is disclosed under the established quashing principles, rather than conclude without analysis that criminality is absent.
